svg.title: 4. Region failover runbook
svg.text: The runbook, with typical timings (rehearsed every quarter in a game day)
Scenario: West Europe goes down during a sale. How the shop moves to North Europe, step by step
Front Door sends every request to
at once; catalog reads are local.
HPA scales pods on RPS, cluster
WAF rate limits and a queue page
failover of the SQL failover group
and of the Cosmos DB write region.
The order outbox in SQL re-sends
Days later, when West Europe is
loss) at low traffic, then Front
origin group: WE p1 · NE p2
forced failover of the SQL failover group and the Cosmos DB write region · RW listener CNAME (TTL 30 s) follows
• About 2 minutes of errors on pages that hit the old region, then the site came back.
• Signed-in sessions in Redis were lost: people signed in again. Carts are in Cosmos DB, so they survived.
• Orders written in the last seconds before the outage may need the outbox replay (RPO > 0, async).
• Checkout was rate limited for ~6 minutes while North Europe scaled. Nobody was charged twice.
RTO 15 min for checkout · RPO ≤ 1 min for orders · 0 for payments (the PSP is the record)
